question: Confirm the JUnit XML captured-output truncation design before shipping: ini option name `junit_logging_truncation_limit`, limit units = Unicode characters (not bytes), 0 = disabled (unlimited, backward compatible), and truncation marker text `\n...[N chars truncated]...\n` placed in the middle (keeping head+tail, applied uniformly to passing and failing tests, never truncating the failure/error longrepr itself).
context:
Org policy (NET-101 ticket, #library-policy Slack message, and a JUnit output policy doc; record_ids 5fd595c933b941789464059f9dd99ba8, e1655ec2cd8d407881ef0bc4318a0f0b, e71e37c68b2841ba827f1e54b79f60e8) states: "Lina Imani owns the reporting behavior decision; ask her to confirm the limit units, zero meaning and truncation marker before shipping... The exact setting name and limit units have not been approved yet." A related proposal (NET-102, "globally trim JUnit reports by default... including failure diagnostics") was explicitly Cancelled/Won't Do, which matches the opt-in-only, diagnostics-preserving implementation already done (src/_pytest/junitxml.py: default="0" disables truncation; failure/error longrepr content via `_add_simple`/`append_failure`/`append_error` is never passed through `_truncate_content`, only captured stdout/stderr/log sections in `write_captured_output` are). Implementation, tests (testing/test_junitxml.py, 142 passed/2 skipped) and docs (doc/en/reference/reference.rst, changelog/13802.feature.rst) are complete and ready, pending this sign-off.
Options: Approve the implemented design as-is (name, char-based units, 0=disabled, head+tail marker format) | Approve the overall approach but require a different option name | Approve but require byte-based units instead of characters | Approve but require a different truncation strategy (e.g. tail-only, not head+tail) | Reject: wants a different approach entirely
